title: Homomorphisms of R-algebras, quotient algebras and powers of ideals
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. An $R$-algebra is a commutative ring $D$ together with a ring homomorphism $R\to D$ (its structure map); a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:A\to B$ is a ring homomorphism with $f\circ(R\to A)=(R\to B)$. For ideals $I,J$ of a commutative ring $D$, $IJ$ is the ideal generated by the products $xy$ ($x\in I$, $y\in J$), $J^0=D$, $J^{k+1}=J^kJ$; $J$ has square zero if $J^2=0$. For an ideal $J$ of an $R$-algebra $D$, the quotient ring $D/J$ is an $R$-algebra through $R\to D\to D/J$, and the quotient map $q:D\to D/J$ is a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras with kernel $J$.
